$comment: Pinned reference measurements for LexiSharp.Eval. Two kinds of assertion live here and they are
regression pins  — the value LexiSharp produces at a fixed configuration. Tight tolerance.
These are the teeth of the net: deterministic, and they catch any change to
scoring, candidate generation, tokenization or metrics.
parity figures   — the independent implementation's number for the same task and index.
A credibility claim with a source, not a guard. |lexisharp - anserini| is
meaningful only where the configuration is genuinely aligned, and the
arguana row is aligned across different BM25 parameters, which is recorded
as such rather than glossed over.
Run --verify-reference to see what moved, then edit expectedNdcg here by hand: --write is
accepted and writes nothing, deliberately. Read the diff before committing it: re-recording is
how a pinned baseline stops catching anything.

The same configuration as arguana/english, counting a repeated query term once per occurrence. Together the two pins bracket what the setting is worth at this k1: 0.289 distinct, 0.271 query-frequency, so +0.018. RE-RECORDED after a fix, and the value it replaces recorded a defect rather than a behaviour. SearchOptions.ExcludedDocumentIds was never applied on the term-at-a-time path, which is the one this query takes on a corpus of 8,674 documents and 645-word queries, so the document being excluded stayed at rank 1 - and for this corpus it is the lexically closest document to the query, because the query text is a document's own text. 0.2864 is what the option produced while doing nothing. Measured after the fix: 0.3806. The seven other nDCG pins and all three index fingerprints are unchanged and the golden master is byte-identical, which is the evidence that the fix reached the path it was aimed at and no other. The same config also publishes recall, which this harness measures but the pin does not yet assert: reference R@100 0.9324, R@1000 0.9872, at k1=0.9, b=0.4. Not asserted here because the pinned metric is nDCG@10 and the recall figures are recorded in the configuration's own results block for a reader who wants them.

indexFingerprints.note: Our index holds 1.12% more terms than the reference index, and the same excess appears on all three corpora - nfcorpus 2.77%, scifact 1.50% - always in the same direction and always inside the 3% tolerance. A systematic excess across three corpora is an analysis difference rather than a corpus quirk. The measured cause is contractions: the reference tokenizer keeps an apostrophe inside a word, so "don't" is one token, where this library's tokenizer produces two - a stem and a single-character fragment such as "t" or "ve", and "it's" yields only the fragment "s". Single-character tokens are 3.4% of this corpus, 6.3% of nfcorpus and 4.5% of scifact, and the excess tracks that ordering. Removing the apostrophe before analysis brings the count to 973,318, which is 0.39% from the reference rather than 1.12%. Whether that also moves the score is a separate measurement; it is not claimed here, and changing the tokenizer would invalidate every recorded baseline.

parity.note: Like for like: 0.3215 measured at the reference's own k1=0.9, b=0.4 under the reference analysis, against 0.3218 published - a difference of -0.0003. 0.327 at this library's default k1/b under the reference analysis. The aligned figure is what belongs in this field, so that one column means one thing across all three rows: the first time this field was written it held the default-parameter figure for this row and the aligned one for ArguAna, which made a difference column computed from it meaningless.

Like for like: 0.6788 measured at the reference's own k1=0.9, b=0.4 under the reference analysis, against 0.6789 published - a difference of -0.0001. 0.692 at this library's default k1/b under the reference analysis. The aligned figure is what belongs in this field, so that one column means one thing across all three rows: the first time this field was written it held the default-parameter figure for this row and the aligned one for ArguAna, which made a difference column computed from it meaningless.

RE-RECORDED, three times over, and every earlier note reached a wrong conclusion. The 0.4061 that was withdrawn rested on a query-frequency setting that was inert through the engine. The 0.2902 that replaced it was written beside a reference of 0.397 measured at k1=0.9, b=0.4, so the two rows were never like for like. What the 0.126 deficit at matched parameters actually was: ExcludedDocumentIds was silently ignored on the term-at-a-time path, the one this corpus takes, and the query's own document - a near-duplicate of the query - was ranked first. With that fixed, at the reference's own k1 and b: 0.364 against 0.397, a deficit of 0.033. At this library's own defaults, k1=1.5 and b=0.75, with the repeated-term setting on, the same run reads 0.444, which is 0.047 above the published figure. ArguAna's score is steep in k1 - 0.290 to 0.381 on the repeated-term setting alone - so the published number was produced at an operating point that appears poor for this corpus, and whether the reference also reads higher there cannot be tested from here. The aligned row above is kept as the honest comparison; this note records that the corpus is not behind. The index fingerprint note records the one measured analysis difference, worth about +0.003.

referenceSource.what: The BM25 figures on the three corpora below, and the index statistics, are the ones Anserini's own BEIR reproduction configs record as the result of their 'bm25' model. They are not transcribed from a paper's table: the configs carry the numbers in a results block next to the command that produced them.
referenceSource.perCorpusConfig: beir-v1.0.0-{arguana,nfcorpus,scifact}.flat.yaml, one file per corpus, each carrying index_stats, the metric command, the model parameters and the results
referenceSource.analyzedIndex: BeirFlatCollection with DefaultLuceneDocumentGenerator: title and text concatenated into one field, as this harness does too
referenceSource.analysis: Lucene EnglishAnalyzer: Porter stemming, its 33-word stop list, single-character terms kept. StopWords.EnglishFunction is word-for-word that list, checked.
referenceSource.parameters: k1=0.9, b=0.4 - not an assumption. The configs pass '-bm25' with no override, and Anserini's own defaults for -bm25.k1 and -bm25.b are 0.9 and 0.4, chosen to follow Trotman et al. (SIGIR 2012 OSIR Workshop). Lucene's own BM25 defaults are 1.2/0.75, so this had to be checked rather than assumed.
referenceSource.queryOwnDocument: REMOVED. The configs pass '-removeQuery', documented as 'Remove docids that have the query id when writing final run output'. So the published ArguAna figure was produced with the query's own document dropped - which is the convention --exclude-query-doc implements, and the reason that gate was a defect here rather than a nicety: 1,298 of ArguAna's 1,406 test queries are corpus documents whose text is the query text.
referenceSource.verifiedOn: Every figure and index statistic above was read back out of the configs on readOn, not carried from an earlier session: 0.3970 / 0.3218 / 0.6789 and 8674/8673/969528, 3633/3633/637485, 5183/5183/838128.
referenceSource.docgenTemplate: beir-v1.0.0-{corpus}.flat.template, which states the index construction in its own words: "These experiments index the corpus in a 'flat' manner, by concatenating the 'title' and 'text' into the 'contents' field." This harness concatenates them the same way, checked rather than assumed.
referenceSource.theBaselineIsNotOneNumber: The 2021 BEIR paper reports BM25 on arguana at 0.315, and indexes the title and passage as SEPARATE text fields through Elasticsearch defaults. Anserini's regression reports 0.3970 for the same corpus at the same k1 and b, indexing title and text concatenated. The two published values are 0.082 apart because they are different indexes. nfcorpus and scifact agree across both, so the arguana row is the one where the choice of published figure changes the conclusion.
referenceSource.noPublishedRunFile: The reproduction directory publishes commands, configs and docgen only - no results, and no per-query trec_run. Attribution of the remaining arguana gap therefore needs that file from outside this repository; it is bounded and characterised here instead.
